beats.say: Now enlarge the layer. A square projection with width four thousand ninety-six contains nearly seventeen million weights. Full fine-tuning can train every one, along with the training state they require.

At rank sixteen, the two factors contain about one hundred thirty-one thousand trainable values altogether. That's less than one percent of the original matrix. The inset magnifies their narrow width.

For any rectangular layer, count the two thin rectangles: rank times input width, plus output width times rank. Increase rank and adapter parameters grow linearly, along with the available update capacity.

Write z equals A x and let g be the loss gradient with respect to the layer output. With scale s, B receives s times the outer product of g and z. A receives s times the outer product of B transpose g and x. These are loss gradients; separate optimizer decay can add another update. The original paper uses Gaussian A; PEFT’s ordinary linear initialization uses Kaiming-uniform A and zero B. These choices preserve the same zero-correction invariant.

At B zero, the A loss gradient is zero. B can move if the scale, incoming gradient and measured intermediate make their outer product nonzero. In our scalar trace, A is one, B is zero, x is one and the target is one. Half squared error gives B gradient minus one. An SGD rate of zero point one makes B zero point one.

The next output is zero point one, so the error is minus zero point nine. Now B gradient is minus zero point nine and A gradient is minus zero point zero nine; both can move. If A x is zero, B waits for that example. If both factors are zero, both loss gradients vanish. Reversing the no-op initialization can make A move first instead, and batch contributions can cancel. Starting both factors nonzero usually changes the checkpoint’s first output.

Count one supplied block with four attention projections of size four thousand ninety-six squared. Its gate and up matrices have widths four thousand ninety-six and eleven thousand eight, while down reverses those dimensions. At rank sixteen, query plus value uses two hundred sixty-two thousand one hundred forty-four adapter parameters.

All four attention adapters plus all three MLP adapters use one million two hundred forty-nine thousand two hundred eighty parameters, about four point seven seven times the query-value budget. Attention changes information routing and content; the MLP transforms each token. The original LoRA work studied query-value and other attention choices. In the QLoRA paper’s Alpaca comparison, spreading adapters across the LLaMA-seven-billion model’s linear layers helped it match full fine-tuning.

Inspect actual module shapes. Our executed tiny Qwen-two fixture has hidden width sixteen, MLP width thirty-two, two query heads and one key-value head. Query-value targeting at rank two costs one hundred twelve parameters, all attention costs two hundred twenty-four, and all seven linear projections cost five hundred twelve. Grouped-query keys and values are narrower here. The output head is excluded by the checked all-linear shortcut.

This tiny Qwen-two model starts with random weights on a CPU. Ask PEFT to attach a rank-two adapter to every linear projection in the block. The seven matches add five hundred twelve adapter parameters, against three thousand four hundred eight original base parameters.

The combined wrapped count is three thousand nine hundred twenty. At first the new branch contributes zero. The base weights stay frozen. Across two steps the gradients reach B first, then A. Save the adapter and reload it onto the same seeded base. The CPU check compares outputs before and after a supported merge.

Read the seven yellow counts. Each one belongs to a projection that received an adapter. For the larger model, set the rank, alpha, dropout, target modules, and causal language modeling task. Print the matched names, shapes, and trainable counts again. Then measure peak memory on the training GPU and score the held-out tickets.

beats.say: Try a fresh scoring layer. Its weights are supplied for this calculation. A negative score keeps a ticket in routine review. Zero or above sends it to the rotation owner. The input is two, one. Use the frozen row for the blue score. Then use A, B and the scale of two. Where will the adapted score land?

The frozen row gives minus two plus one, or minus one. On the other path, two minus a half leaves one and a half. B halves that to three quarters. Scaling by two gives a correction of one and a half. Add that to the blue score and you land at positive one half. Send this ticket to the rotation owner.

Now pull out the two sets we reserved. These are separate, fictional evaluation results. On the twenty policy tickets the candidate gets nineteen correct. On the routine reviews it gets eighteen correct. Look at ticket seven. Its key was only twelve days old, yet the assistant sent it to the owner. That second set falls below ninety-five percent. Hold this candidate. Keep the clean base and the separate adapter so you can inspect the missed replies.

Two follow-up candidates each fix exactly one ticket. Candidate A fixes policy ticket twenty. Candidate B fixes routine ticket seven instead. Everything else matches the original run. Which candidate gets at least nineteen right in both sets?

Try A first. Policy ticket twenty moves to the rotation owner. Its row is now perfect. The two missed routine reviews are still there. A gets thirty-eight correct overall, but routine reviews stay at eighteen. Hold A.

Go back to the original answers and try B. Ticket seven returns to routine review. That brings routine reviews up to nineteen, alongside nineteen on policy. Both candidates got thirty-eight right. Only B passes the release rule. Keep that adapter with the exact base and ticket format you tested. To resume training after preemption, keep the optimizer state, schedule and data position too. Training Run Operations picks up there, with global batch size and learning-rate scaling.

changed.previousSay: Try a fresh supplied scalar layer representing a fictional escalation score. The base row is minus one, one. A is one, minus zero point five; B is zero point five. Rank is one, alpha is two, and the new request vector is two, one. A nonnegative score means escalate. Predict the base score, the adapter correction and the final decision. These authored weights are a calculation, not a fitted policy model. Pause.

The base dot product is minus two plus one, or minus one. A measures two minus zero point five, giving one point five. Multiplying by B gives zero point seven five, and the scale two makes the correction one point five. Adding it produces zero point five, so this supplied request changes from do not escalate to escalate. Every result uses the same request and same factors.

Now apply a separate, predeclared evaluation rule. The candidate must reach at least ninety-five percent on each twenty-case set. Its supplied policy results are nineteen correct, while regression results are eighteen. Policy reaches ninety-five percent; regression reaches ninety and fails. Keep the candidate out of that deployment despite the correct changed request. Preserve the clean base and adapter, diagnose those missed cases, and make the next controlled change. A useful small path has to earn both its new behavior and its retained capabilities. Next, take this adapter training job into Training Run Operations. The job now needs to recover from preemption while keeping global batch and learning-rate scaling consistent.

All four attention adapters plus all three MLP adapters use one million two hundred forty-nine thousand two hundred eighty parameters, about four point seven seven times the query-value budget. Attention changes information routing and content; the MLP transforms each token. The original LoRA work studied query-value and other attention choices. The article executes a real PEFT wrapper on a tiny randomly initialized Qwen-two model, using PyTorch two point thirteen, Transformers five point sixteen point one and PEFT zero point twenty. It downloads no checkpoint. With all-linear rank two, it verifies seven matched projections and five hundred twelve adapter parameters, against three thousand four hundred eight original base parameters.

The combined wrapped count is three thousand nine hundred twenty. The fixture checks that initialization preserves base output, base parameters stay frozen, and gradients reach the factors in the expected order across two steps. It saves the adapter, reloads the same seeded base with that adapter, and compares outputs before and after a supported merge.

This is a CPU implementation contract, not evidence of policy accuracy, a seven-billion-model training run or GPU memory fit. For the larger job, specify rank, alpha, target modules, dropout and causal-language-model task type, then inspect actual matches and trainable counts. A shortcut earns trust through its resolved modules and shapes.
